name: History & Geography
description: Journey across world capitals, landmarks, and historic milestones across 11 levels.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was founded as a compromise capital between rivals Sydney and Melbourne in 1908.

questions.question: What is traditionally considered the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River spans approximately 6,650 km (4,132 miles) through northeastern Africa.

questions.question: Which country has the largest total land area in the world?
questions.explanation: Russia covers over 17.1 million square kilometers across Europe and Asia.

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain peak on Earth above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest in the Himalayas stands at 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet).

questions.question: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa was chosen as Canada's capital by Queen Victoria in 1857.

questions.question: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.explanation: Africa contains 54 fully recognized sovereign nations.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.explanation: Tokyo has been the capital and seat of the Emperor since 1868.

questions.question: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert in North Africa covers roughly 9.2 million square kilometers.

questions.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.explanation: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as the federal capital in 1960.

questions.question: Which island is the largest island in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Greenland covers about 2.16 million square kilometers.

questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the Great Pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Dynasty pharaohs of Ancient Egypt erected the Giza pyramids ~2500 BCE.

questions.question: Which two rivers defined the ancient region of Mesopotamia?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia literally means 'between rivers' in Greek, referring to the Tigris and Euphrates.

questions.question: Who was the first Emperor of the Roman Empire?
questions.explanation: Octavian took the title Augustus in 27 BCE, becoming Rome's inaugural emperor.

questions.question: What ancient civilization is credited with inventing the wheel and cuneiform writing?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians of lower Mesopotamia developed cuneiform and the wheel around 3500 BCE.

questions.question: Which famous Greek philosopher was the teacher of Alexander the Great?
questions.explanation: Aristotle was hired by King Philip II of Macedon to tutor his young son Alexander.

questions.question: In which modern-day country did the ancient Indus Valley Civilization flourish?
questions.explanation: Major sites like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are situated along the Indus River basin in Pakistan and northwest India.

questions.question: Who was the first Emperor of a unified China who built the Terracotta Army?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang united China in 221 BCE and ordered the Terracotta Army buried with him.

questions.question: Which ancient city was famously destroyed by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE?
questions.explanation: Pompeii and neighboring Herculaneum were buried under pumice and volcanic ash in 79 CE.

questions.question: What ancient legal code is famous for the principle 'an eye for an eye'?
questions.explanation: King Hammurabi of Babylon promulgated his comprehensive legal code around 1754 BCE.

questions.question: Which ancient Wonder of the World was located in Alexandria, Egypt?
questions.explanation: The Pharos of Alexandria was a lighthouse built by the Ptolemaic Kingdom ~280 BCE.

questions.question: In which year was the Magna Carta signed by King John of England?
questions.explanation: Barons compelled King John to seal the Magna Carta at Runnymede in June 1215.

questions.question: What devastating pandemic killed an estimated 30-60% of Europe's population in the 14th century?
questions.explanation: The Black Death (bubonic plague) ravaged Europe between 1346 and 1353.

questions.question: Who founded the vast Mongol Empire in the early 13th century?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan united nomadic tribes in 1206 to establish the largest contiguous land empire in history.

questions.question: What was the capital of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire?
questions.explanation: Constantinople (modern Istanbul) was the vibrant heart of the Byzantine Empire until 1453.

questions.question: In what year did Constantinople fall to the Ottoman Empire led by Sultan Mehmed II?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453 marked the end of the Byzantine Empire.

questions.question: Which famous battle took place in England in 1066 leading to the Norman Conquest?
questions.explanation: William the Conqueror defeated King Harold II at the Battle of Hastings in October 1066.

questions.question: Who was the French peasant girl who led the royal army during the Hundred Years' War?
questions.explanation: Joan of Arc lifted the Siege of Orléans in 1429 before being martyred in 1431.

questions.question: Which European traveler spent 24 years traveling across Asia and served Kublai Khan?
questions.explanation: Venetian merchant Marco Polo documented Asian geography and culture in 'The Travels of Marco Polo'.

questions.question: What famous Moroccan scholar traveled over 73,000 miles across the Islamic world in the 14th century?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta visited North Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, India, and China.

questions.question: Which dynasty ruled the Aztec Empire until the Spanish conquest led by Hernán Cortés?
questions.explanation: Hernán Cortés captured Tenochtitlan and conquered the Aztec Empire in 1521.

questions.question: In what year did Christopher Columbus first make landfall in the Americas?
questions.explanation: Columbus landed in the Bahamas on October 12, 1492, under the sponsorship of Spain.

questions.question: Which Portuguese explorer was the first European to reach India by sea around the Cape of Good Hope?
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode), India, in May 1498.

questions.question: Whose expedition was the first to successfully circumnavigate the globe (1519-1522)?
questions.explanation: Magellan initiated the voyage; Juan Sebastián Elcano completed it after Magellan died in the Philippines.

questions.question: Which continent is named after the Italian explorer Amerigo Vespucci?
questions.explanation: Cartographer Martin Waldseemüller named the new continents 'America' on his 1507 world map.

questions.question: Which English explorer famously circumnavigated the globe aboard the Golden Hind between 1577 and 1580?
questions.explanation: Drake was knighted by Queen Elizabeth I for his round-the-world privateering voyage.

questions.question: Which treaty signed in 1494 divided newly discovered lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Tordesillas drew a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands.

questions.question: Who was the British naval captain that mapped New Zealand and the eastern coast of Australia in the 1770s?
questions.explanation: Captain Cook undertook three Pacific voyages on the HMS Endeavour and Resolution.

questions.question: Which explorer discovered the Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River in 1855?
questions.explanation: Scottish missionary David Livingstone named the falls in honor of Queen Victoria.

questions.question: Who led the first expedition to reach the geographic South Pole in December 1911?
questions.explanation: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole 34 days ahead of Captain Scott.

questions.question: Who was the first person to set foot on the summit of Mount Everest in May 1953 alongside Tenzing Norgay?
questions.explanation: Sir Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on May 29, 1953.

questions.question: What is the deepest known oceanic trench on planet Earth?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench reaches approximately 10,994 meters (36,070 feet).

questions.question: Which river flows through the largest rainforest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon River basin contains the vast Amazon Rainforest across South America.

questions.question: In which country is the famous archaeological citadel of Machu Picchu located?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu is an Incan citadel built in the 15th century high in the Andes mountains of Peru.

questions.question: What is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls (Salto Ángel) in Venezuela has a plunge of 979 meters (3,212 feet).

questions.question: What body of water separates the United Kingdom from mainland Europe?
questions.explanation: The English Channel connects the North Sea to the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake by volume in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia contains about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.

questions.question: What strait connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar lies between southern Spain and northern Morocco.

questions.question: Which African country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is an enclaved landlocked high-altitude country encircled by South Africa.

questions.question: What is the longest mountain range on land on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Andes stretch over 7,000 kilometers along the western edge of South America.

questions.question: Which country has the most natural islands in the world?
questions.explanation: Sweden has over 267,000 islands, more than any other nation on Earth.

questions.question: The assassination of which figure in June 1914 triggered the outbreak of World War I?
questions.explanation: Gavrilo Princip assassinated Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914.

questions.question: In which year did World War I officially end with the armistice?
questions.explanation: Hostilities ceased on the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month in 1918.

questions.question: Which US naval base was attacked by Japan on December 7, 1941, bringing the US into World War II?
questions.explanation: The surprise attack on Pearl Harbor in Hawaii prompted the United States to declare war on Japan.

questions.question: On which French beaches did Allied troops land during the D-Day invasion on June 6, 1944?
questions.explanation: Operation Overlord landed Allied forces across five beach sectors in Normandy.

questions.question: In which two Japanese cities were atomic bombs dropped in August 1945?
questions.explanation: The atomic detonations on Hiroshima (Aug 6) and Nagasaki (Aug 9) precipitated Japan's surrender.

questions.question: What international peacekeeping organization was founded in October 1945 following WWII?
questions.explanation: The UN was chartered in San Francisco by 50 nations to prevent future global conflicts.

questions.question: What symbolic barrier divided East and West Berlin from 1961 until its fall in 1989?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall was erected by East Germany in August 1961 and fell in November 1989.

questions.question: Who was the British Prime Minister that led the UK through most of World War II?
questions.explanation: Churchill delivered iconic speeches and wartime leadership from 1940 to 1945.

questions.question: In what year did the Soviet Union officially dissolve?
questions.explanation: The USSR was formally dissolved on December 26, 1991, creating 15 independent nations.

questions.question: What military alliance was established by Western nations in 1949 for collective defense?
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization was formed to counter Soviet expansionism.

questions.question: Who led the nonviolent Salt March in India in 1930 to protest British salt taxes?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi led the 240-mile Dandi March, galvanizing the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: Who served 27 years in prison before becoming South Africa's first Black president in 1994?
questions.explanation: Nelson Mandela won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 and led the post-apartheid transition.

questions.question: Which American President issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863?
questions.explanation: Lincoln declared all enslaved individuals in Confederate states to be forever free.

questions.question: Who was the legendary queen of Egypt who allied with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony?
questions.explanation: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt.

questions.question: Which Russian monarch founded the city of Saint Petersburg in 1703?
questions.explanation: Tsar Peter the Great established Saint Petersburg as a European-facing seaport capital.

questions.question: In what year did the storming of the Bastille mark the start of the French Revolution?
questions.explanation: Parisian revolutionaries stormed the Bastille fortress on July 14, 1789.

questions.question: Who was the civil rights leader who delivered the historic 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963?
questions.explanation: Dr. King delivered his speech on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to be elected Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in 1979?
questions.explanation: Known as the 'Iron Lady', Margaret Thatcher served as UK Prime Minister until 1990.

questions.question: What famous treaty officially ended the American Revolutionary War in 1783?
questions.explanation: Great Britain recognized American independence in the Treaty of Paris of 1783.

questions.question: Which Roman general crossed the Rubicon river in 49 BCE, igniting a civil war?
questions.explanation: Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon marked the irreversible plunge into Roman civil war.

questions.question: What is the smallest independent sovereign state in the world by land area and population?
questions.explanation: Vatican City covers just 0.49 square kilometers (121 acres) in the heart of Rome.

questions.question: Which country shares the longest international land border in the world with another country?
questions.explanation: The US-Canada border stretches 8,891 kilometers (5,525 miles).

questions.question: What is the only continent that contains no sovereign countries?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is governed by the Antarctic Treaty System dedicated to scientific research.

questions.question: Which city is known as the highest capital city in the world above sea level?
questions.explanation: La Paz sits at roughly 3,640 meters (11,942 feet) above sea level.

questions.question: Which African nation was never colonized during the 'Scramble for Africa'?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia successfully defended its sovereignty against colonial Italian invasion at Adwa in 1896.

questions.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.explanation: Ankara became Turkey's capital in 1923 under Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, succeeding Istanbul.

questions.question: How many total landlocked countries are there on the continent of South America?
questions.explanation: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only two landlocked countries in South America.

questions.question: Which country has the longest total coastline in the world?
questions.explanation: Canada has over 243,000 kilometers of coastline spanning three oceans.

questions.question: What is the capital city of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Wellington is the world's southernmost sovereign capital city.

questions.question: Which European nation has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh?
questions.explanation: Switzerland recognizes all four linguistic groups constitutionally.

questions.question: In which Indian city is the iconic white marble Taj Mahal situated?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in Agra in 1632 for his wife Mumtaz.

questions.question: Which massive stone fortification was constructed across northern China to defend against invasions?
questions.explanation: Sections of the Great Wall stretch thousands of kilometers, extensively rebuilt by the Ming dynasty.

questions.question: In which European city will you find the ancient amphitheater known as the Colosseum?
questions.explanation: The Flavian Amphitheatre (Colosseum) in Rome was completed around 80 CE.

questions.question: What famous prehistoric stone circle monument is located in Wiltshire, England?
questions.explanation: Stonehenge's ring of standing megaliths dates back to between 3000 and 2000 BCE.

questions.question: Which grand bell tower and clock is located at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London?
questions.explanation: Big Ben is the nickname of the Great Bell inside Elizabeth Tower in London.

questions.question: In which country is the archaeological rock-cut rose city of Petra located?
questions.explanation: Petra was the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom, famous for its carved sandstone facade, Al-Khazneh.

questions.question: Which iron lattice monument was erected in Paris as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair?
questions.explanation: Gustave Eiffel designed the 330-meter tower, now France's most iconic symbol.

questions.question: What colossal neoclassical sculpture stands on Liberty Island in New York Harbor?
questions.explanation: The statue was a gift from France to the United States, dedicated in 1886.

questions.question: In which country is the ancient temple complex of Angkor Wat located?
questions.explanation: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest religious monument in the world, built by the Khmer Empire.

questions.question: On which mountain in South Dakota are the faces of four US presidents carved?
questions.explanation: Mount Rushmore depicts Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Lincoln.

questions.question: What year saw the maiden voyage and sinking of the passenger liner RMS Titanic?
questions.explanation: Titanic struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic and sank on April 15, 1912.

questions.question: Which two Apollo 11 astronauts walked on the Moon on July 20, 1969?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent over two hours exploring Tranquility Base.

questions.question: In what year did the Chernobyl nuclear disaster occur in Soviet Ukraine?
questions.explanation: Reactor No. 4 exploded on April 26, 1986, during a safety test.

questions.question: Which international treaty entered into force in 1993 establishing the European Union?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty integrated European communities into the European Union.

questions.question: In what year did the Panama Canal officially open, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans?
questions.explanation: The 82-kilometer canal officially opened to commercial traffic on August 15, 1914.

questions.question: What international trade agreement between the US, Canada, and Mexico was enacted in 1994?
questions.explanation: The North American Free Trade Agreement eliminated trade tariffs among the three nations.

questions.question: Who was the Soviet leader who introduced the policies of 'Glasnost' (openness) and 'Perestroika' (restructuring)?
questions.explanation: Gorbachev's reforms inadvertently accelerated the disintegration of the Soviet bloc.

questions.question: In what year did Hong Kong sovereignty transfer from the United Kingdom to China?
questions.explanation: The handover concluded 156 years of British colonial rule on July 1, 1997.

questions.question: Which organization was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for efforts to combat hunger worldwide?
questions.explanation: The UN World Food Programme provides food assistance to over 100 million people annually.

questions.question: In what year was the euro physical currency notes and coins introduced into circulation?
questions.explanation: Euro banknotes and coins officially entered public circulation across 12 nations on January 1, 2002.

questions.question: What is the world's largest salt flat, located in southwestern Bolivia?
questions.explanation: Salar de Uyuni covers over 10,500 square kilometers and holds vast reserves of lithium.

questions.question: Which body of water has a surface and shore that is Earth's lowest elevation on land?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea shores sit about 430 meters (1,410 feet) below sea level.

questions.question: What is the driest non-polar desert on Earth, located in northern Chile?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Atacama Desert have had no recorded rainfall for centuries.

questions.question: Which strait separates the southern tip of South America from Antarctica?
questions.explanation: The Drake Passage connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans through notoriously rough waters.

questions.question: What is the largest inland sea (often termed a saltwater lake) on Earth by area?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea covers roughly 371,000 square kilometers between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: What is the name of the active stratovolcano that forms the highest peak in Japan?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji stands at 3,776 meters and is a sacred UNESCO Cultural World Heritage site.

questions.question: Which European capital city is built on an archipelago of 14 islands connected by over 50 bridges?
questions.explanation: Stockholm, capital of Sweden, is situated across Lake Mälaren and the Baltic Sea.

questions.question: What is the most populous city in the world by urban metropolitan area?
questions.explanation: The Greater Tokyo Area encompasses over 37 million residents.

questions.question: Which canal connects the Mediterranean Sea directly to the Red Sea, opening in 1869?
questions.explanation: Ferdinand de Lesseps supervised construction of the 193-kilometer Suez Canal in Egypt.

questions.question: What country has the most time zones, counting all overseas territories?
questions.explanation: France spans 12 different time zones across its mainland and global overseas territories.
